caption: Cornish-Adebiyi v. Caesars Entertainment, Inc.
citation_line: Cornish-Adebiyi v. Caesars Entertainment, Inc., No. 1:23-cv-02536, ECF No. 139 (D.N.J. Sept. 30, 2024), rev’d, No. 24-3006 (3d Cir. July 29, 2026)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Williams dismissed a putative antitrust class action alleging that Atlantic City casino-hotels used Cendyn’s AI-driven dynamic-pricing software to coordinate room rates, finding the complaint did not plausibly plead the “rim” of a hub-and-spoke conspiracy.
qualification_rationale: The case is a leading modern test of how traditional Sherman Act pleading rules apply to competitors’ use of a shared pricing algorithm and exchange of nonpublic commercial data.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit reversed and remanded in a precedential opinion on July 29, 2026. Taking the allegations as true, it held that the complaint plausibly alleged a horizontal agreement facilitated by the shared algorithm; it did not decide ultimate liability.
